title: In eye-column coordinates, ON (T4) and OFF (T5) motion-detector input directions agree at each column and between two fly connectomes, and their position-dependent deviations repeat
abstract: Question: Does the input wiring direction of fly T4 (ON) and T5 (OFF) motion detectors follow the eye-column grid in the same way in both pathways and in different flies? Approach: For each cell we used the synapse rule of sci:d115ed1d (centroid of Mi4 minus Mi9 inputs for T4, CT1 minus Tm9 for T5) and expressed it in local hexagonal column units. We used two complete connectomes: FlyWire v783 (female, TEM, 10,525 cells) and male CNS v1.0 (male, FIB-SEM, 13,426 cells), both eyes, all eight subtypes. Results: At the same column, T4 and T5 of one subtype pointed in the same lattice direction (mean difference -4.0 to +2.6 degrees in 16 groups; -13.8 to +10.4 degrees in a brain-axis frame). Subtype mean angles of the two flies differed by a median of 1.1 degrees in the lattice frame (maximum 3.3) and 4.5 degrees in the brain-axis frame (maximum 13.8). Deviations from the subtype mean were shared by T4 and T5 at a column (smoothed circular correlation 0.41 to 0.81; null 95% at most 0.18) and repeated across eyes and flies (mean map correlation 0.56 between flies, 0.59 within a fly, 0.21 for displaced alignments). This was strongest for subtypes c and d (between flies r 0.61 to 0.76, p = 0.016 in all comparisons) and weaker for a and b. The local physical lattice frame raised angle concentration in all 32 groups, but a lattice displaced by 4 to 10 columns gave 37% (FlyWire) and 60% (male CNS) of the gain, so local grid distortion explains only part of the brain-frame spatial pattern. Interpretation: a stereotyped, eye-position-dependent direction map is shared by the ON and OFF pathways and by two flies. Limitations: anatomy only, no recordings; two animals with sex and imaging method confounded; approximate eye alignment; male CNS T4/T5 columns from the strongest Mi1/Tm1 input; angles within the lattice depend on the ideal hex embedding; no eye micro-CT.
